newsitem.title: CHINA: New HK chief vows to keep world's "freest economy".
newsitem.headline: New HK chief vows to keep world's "freest economy".

text.p: Hong Kong, as part of China, intends to remain "the world's freest and most vibrant economy" in a new era marked by democracy, Chief Executive Tung Chee-hwa said on Tuesday, unveiling his political agenda.

The south China city's new leader issued a rallying call to the 6.4 million population to develop skills in this region, which lacks natural resources, and fend off challenges to Hong Kong's place as the world's seventh trading economy.
He pledged a 10-year drive to boost public housing and combat land speculation, and pledged to develop education and ways of enhancing free trade, key to Hong Kong's success.
Speaking soon after he took over on the first day under Beijing's rule, Tung declared: "Democracy is the hallmark of a new era for Hong Kong."

The 60-year-old Shanghai-born ex-shipping magnate, who replaced colonial governor Chris Patten, faces public uncertainty about his commitment to civil rights, as reflected in a slipping popularity rating in opinion polls.
His remarks appeared to be aimed at soothing anxieties among pro-democracy campaigners here and in the West that he places a higher emphasis on social order and responsibility over liberal values.

He spoke at an inauguration ceremony of his new government when China's President Jiang Zemin declared that Beijing wanted Hong Kong to remain free and prosperous as an autonomous region of the People's Republic of China.
Hours after it was sworn in, the Beijing-appointed legislature passed an omnibus bill activating laws curbing protests and the funding of political parties.
Pro-democracy activists promptly vowed to stage more protests in Hong Kong and called on communist China to hold immediate legislative elections.
Democracy campaigners and Western leaders have been angered by disbandment of the popularly-elected legislative council until elections promised in a year's time.
But Tung pledged: "We will preserve existing freedoms and lifestyle."
